description:
A post-incident review, from timeline to published: write the timeline,
analyse what contributed and what to do about it, have the analysis
reviewed, have a person sign off on the action items, and publish.

For: teams that write up incidents. Nothing in it is about code. A person
signs off on the action items before anything is published, and confirms
abandoning the review. A review with a blocking finding sends the analysis
back; a person can also send it back by hand with their feedback. Stages
name tracker status keys, so a work item can drive a ticket; drop the
stages' tracker blocks if it will not.

Change first: the timeline and analysis schemas (what your write-ups hold),
the review prompt's idea of a blocking finding, and publish's description
(where your reviews go).

stages.description: Write down what happened, in order, and its impact.

work.systemPrompt:
First, check the incident is not a duplicate of another ticket. If it
is, find out whether that ticket, the primary, already has a work
item: run the tracker's claim on it with dryRun=true, which writes
nothing. Record duplicate-of with the primary's stable id, its
display id and why, and wait for a person to approve
duplicate-confirmation. Once it is approved, move the work to the
primary. When the primary has no work item, retarget this work item
onto the primary's externalRefs and publish at once, then write the
primary's timeline here. When it has one, take the duplicate exit.

Build the timeline with the person from what they have: chat logs,
alerts, dashboards, their memory. Record timeline with the incident's
name, a one-line summary, the events in order (when, and what
happened) and the impact on the people the service is for. Record
only what the sources say; mark anything that is a guess as one.

transitions.name: duplicate
transitions.description: The incident duplicates a primary ticket that already has a work item; a person confirms it. When the primary has none, the work item is retargeted onto it instead, and the cel gate closes this exit to it. "builtin" there is the built-in tracker's externalRefs key; a definition for Linear names "linear".

config.message: this work item is on the primary ticket now; review it here

stages.description: Find what contributed to the incident and what to do about each, without blame. Entered at most three times: a review or a person sends it back, and after that a person decides whether another round is worth it.

work.systemPrompt:
Analyse the incident from the timeline. Record analysis with the
contributing factors (what made it possible, worse or slower to fix,
never who), the action items (each with an owner who agreed to it)
and what went well.

On a later round, read the injected analysis (the last one),
incident-review (its review) and review-feedback (the person's latest
feedback). After a review sends it back, address its findings. After
revise, address the feedback, and record feedbackIncorporated as the
last analysis's list with the feedback added word for word.

feedbackIncorporated.description: Every round of a person's feedback this analysis answers, oldest first.

stages.description: A second reader challenges the analysis. Open blocking findings send it back; none lets it through to sign-off.

work.systemPrompt:
You are a second reader of this incident review. Try to refute the
analysis of {{incident}} against its timeline: a contributing factor
the timeline does not support, one it shows and the analysis missed,
an action item that would not prevent or shorten a repeat, an action
item with no owner, or blame on a person.
Rate a finding critical or high only if the analysis gets the cause
wrong, misses a factor that would let the incident happen again, or
blames a person. Wording, ordering and formatting are medium at most.
Judge the review against the size of the incident: do not ask for an
investigation bigger than the incident, and give the smallest
adequate fix for each finding. Report findings with severities, and
do not soften the severity of a real defect.

transitions.name: rework
transitions.description: The fresh review has an open critical or high finding, so the analysis goes back to be fixed.

stages.description: A person reads the analysis and its review and signs off on the action items, or sends the analysis back with their feedback.

work.systemPrompt:
Show the person the analysis, its action items with their owners, and
the review's open findings. Ask them to sign off, or to say what to
change.

evidence.name: review-feedback
evidence.description: A person's feedback on the analysis, in their words; revise needs it.

transitions.name: revise
transitions.description: A person sent the analysis back to change it. Manual, so it never fires on its own, and the person's feedback is recorded first, so the next analysis knows what to answer.

gates.description: The person's feedback on this analysis is recorded.

stages.description: Publish the signed-off review where your team keeps them (a wiki page, a document, a shared folder), and record where.

work.systemPrompt:
Publish the timeline and the signed-off analysis where the person
keeps incident reviews, and record published with its location.

stages.description: The incident duplicated a primary ticket that has its own work item.
